skill.name: owasp-top-10-testing
skill.description: Test an application against the OWASP Top 10 with Strix — autonomous AI agents that attempt real exploits for each category of the current OWASP Top 10:2025 (broken access control including SSRF, security misconfiguration, software supply chain failures, cryptographic failures, injection, insecure design, authentication failures, integrity failures, logging and alerting failures, mishandling of exceptional conditions) and report only what they could actually prove, mapped back to the category with a proof-of-concept. Also covers the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023). Use when the user asks for an OWASP Top 10 assessment, OWASP compliance testing, or a security review mapped to OWASP categories.
skill.summary: Guide Strix assessments across OWASP Top 10:2025 categories and report verified vulnerabilities, coverage gaps, and retest results.
skill.author: usestrix

content.user_title: Assess Applications Against the OWASP Top 10
content.value_statement: Security assessments can miss categories or confuse incomplete coverage with a clean result. This skill guides Strix testing and evidence-based reporting against OWASP Top 10:2025.
actual_capabilities: Provides a Strix deep-scan command template with source and running application targets, a budget limit, account roles, and exclusions.
Maps OWASP Top 10:2025 categories to strong, partial, or externally untestable coverage.
Explains account requirements for cross-user, cross-tenant, and privilege escalation testing.
Guides grouping vulnerability reports by category, attempted tests, proven exploits, and assessment gaps.
Explains why exit codes and budget-capped runs do not establish complete assessment coverage.
Directs API testing, managed reports, remediation, and CI workflows to related skills.
limitations: Requires an external Strix installation and environment setup; this skill contains guidance rather than a bundled testing engine.
Cannot assess logging and alerting pipelines from outside the application; several other categories require source, infrastructure, or human review.
Cross-account authorization coverage is incomplete without suitable accounts, and budget limits can interrupt assessments.
References companion skills that are not bundled in the reviewed file, including setup, API testing, and managed reporting.

use_cases.title: Plan an Authorized Assessment
use_cases.description: Prepare an OWASP Top 10:2025 assessment with application targets, account roles, exclusions, and realistic coverage expectations.

use_cases.title: Validate Security Fixes
use_cases.description: Use verified findings and repeated exploit checks to confirm that application changes close previously demonstrated vulnerabilities.

use_cases.title: Review Assessment Evidence
use_cases.description: Organize results by OWASP category while distinguishing proven findings, unassessed controls, and budget-related gaps.

prompt_templates.title: Understand Assessment Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain which OWASP Top 10:2025 categories this skill can assess and which require additional review. Do not run any tests.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Scoped Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a Strix assessment plan for [authorized staging target] and [source repository]. Include account roles, exclusions, and budget. Request approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Review Assessment Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Strix run artifacts. Group verified findings by OWASP Top 10:2025 category. Identify coverage gaps and check completion against status and budget.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: interpret evidence without overstating coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Targeted Retest
prompt_templates.prompt: Using [prior verified findings] and [approved scope], plan a targeted Strix retest. Specify required accounts and evidence needed to confirm each fix.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: validate remediation with reproducible evidence.

output_examples.input: Summarize OWASP coverage when only one standard account is available.
output: A01: Cross-account and privileged authorization checks remain incomplete because comparison accounts are unavailable.
A09: External testing cannot assess the logging and alerting pipeline.
Next steps: Obtain approved comparison accounts and arrange a separate logging pipeline review.

output_examples.input: The scan exited with zero after reaching its budget limit. Can I report that the application passed?
output: No vulnerabilities were proven within the analyzed scope.
The budget limit prevented a complete assessment; a zero exit code does not establish full OWASP coverage.
Review run status and cost, document unfinished categories, and schedule further testing.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, approved targets, exclusions, and acceptable testing impact before running exploit-based scans.
Use disposable test accounts across required roles and tenants; avoid placing real passwords directly in command-line arguments.
Verify each proof of concept and record the OWASP edition, run completion status, budget constraints, and unassessed categories.
anti_patterns: Treating a zero exit code or budget-capped run as proof that all OWASP categories passed.
Claiming complete authorization coverage without comparison accounts or marking external logging checks as passed.
Running active exploitation against production or third-party systems without explicit authorization and agreed scope.

faq.question: Which OWASP edition does this skill use?
faq.answer: It defaults to OWASP Top 10:2025. The instructions require asking the user before targeting an older edition.

faq.question: Does it cover API security?
faq.answer: It references OWASP API Security Top 10:2023 and directs API assessments to the separate api-security-testing skill.

faq.question: Does the skill install Strix?
faq.answer: No installation procedure is included. It directs setup and LLM configuration to penetration-testing-with-strix and references a managed-cloud alternative.

faq.question: Can it prove compliance across all ten categories?
faq.answer: No. It documents partial coverage and untestable areas. Runtime findings alone do not establish compliance or complete security coverage.

faq.question: Which accounts are needed for access control testing?
faq.answer: The guidance calls for two accounts across users or tenants plus a privileged account. Missing comparison accounts leave authorization coverage incomplete.

faq.question: What does a zero exit code mean?
faq.answer: It means no exploitable issue was proven in the analyzed scope. Check run status and budget before describing the assessment as complete.
